exemplars.title: ReaLJam: Real-Time Human-AI Music Jamming with Reinforcement Learning-Tuned Transformers
exemplars.why: The continually refreshed visual anticipation is the clearest evidence that a forthcoming plan remains visible and relevant while execution unfolds, directly satisfying the pattern’s distinctive persistence requirement.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over DreamGarden because its evidence explicitly couples a visible plan to ongoing execution, whereas DreamGarden clearly establishes plan editing but not execution advancing through the displayed structure.

exemplars.title: Demonstrating DreamGarden: A Designer Assistant for Growing Games from a Single Prompt
exemplars.why: Its node-based action-plan tree is a concrete, persistent planning object that users can prune and expand, making planned operations inspectable and consequentially editable rather than merely announced.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over DELEGACT because the tree editor more clearly makes the plan itself a durable, structured interface object, while DELEGACT more clearly demonstrates validation and commitment but not persistence during execution.

exemplars.title: Learning to Delegate and Act with DELEGACT: Multimodal Language Models for Task-Level Human Cobot Planning in Industrial Assembly
exemplars.why: Editable atomic-task allocations, explicit validation, step-by-step instructions, and individually triggered cobot actions form the strongest evidenced preview-to-commit sequence, with unusually meaningful consequences for what physically executes.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over Cocoa because DELEGACT specifies the plan’s task-level structure, validation boundary, generated instructions, and execution trigger, while Cocoa’s quote establishes only that an initial plan can be edited.

notes: I departed from the consensus by excluding its top-ranked candidate, SketchGPT (rid 13606): its quote establishes task preview and selective authorization, but not an ordered plan, persistence during execution, or progress through the displayed structure. I elevated ReaLJam above DreamGarden because continual visual anticipation supplies the strongest direct evidence for the structural signature’s persistence requirement. DELEGACT remains third despite its narrower industrial setting because its evidence describes a more complete preview–edit–validate–execute workflow than the more general Cocoa. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. All three records rely on short excerpts: DreamGarden and DELEGACT do not explicitly establish that the plan stays visible or marks progress during execution, while ReaLJam does not establish editability, ordering, or commitment-state encoding. Readers should therefore treat those unquoted details as unsupported rather than implied. The lower-ranked in-car assistant may encode plan-plus-progress especially well, but its quotation is truncated and cannot securely establish the exact interface structure.
